title: Crosswind Council
logline: No law on the hill covers the egg — a wish is the largest key ever cut, and Mr. BaneWAP wants it filed, appraised, and auctioned to himself.
epigraph: A key may be filed smaller in the open. It may never be grown in the dark.
description: Chapter 4 of Lore.Land: Crosswind Council. Boof carries the unspent wish to the hilltop table, where a bitter pie in a banker's crust argues it should be filed and auctioned — and the mirror shows every delegate what wanting becomes when it hoards.

content.text: Council Hill kept a great slab of split pine that refused to pick a side, and it was there, under crosswind weather, that Boof brought the egg to be argued over. She slipped beneath the trestle, chin on the timber, and found herself nose to frame with the

children.text: —an upright pane of polished weather that returned not your face but the exact shape of your wanting. Above her, the law of the hill was recited as it had been recited for generations: every permission in Boon.land is a key, iron or brass, and a key may be filed smaller in the open, before witnesses, with the shavings swept into the common bin. A key may never be grown in secret. The Genie stood at the table's edge, hands folded, and added the one fact that mattered: a wish is the largest key ever cut. It opens the momentum of the world itself. That was when the bane-side chair creaked.

content.text: The bitter pie arrived by hired cart, lattice crust tight over berries he'd kept too long. He offered nobody a slice. The wish, he proposed, should be valued, filed, and sold to someone prepared to bear its considerable responsibilities. He paused to let the council imagine such a person. Then supplied his own name.

content.text: The Fool’s Mirror shimmered with the fury of the split sky. It whispered in a tone like wind through eaves: "What you see is not what is, but what your wanting is becoming." The delegates looked, one by one. The boon-side saw their small wants, snug as filed keys. Mr. BaneWAP looked longest, and the glass returned him honestly: every berry he had ever hoarded, pressed airless under crust, gone from sweet to bitter for want of being served. He was not a villain from elsewhere. He was the mirror of what wanting becomes when it stops handing out slices. The egg, reflected beside him, showed no bidder's number and no bounding box — a wish keeps its own law, and no appraisal on the hill could get purchase on its shell.

content.text: Every court gets a vizier. I sampled that trope, folks — and honked it back as pastry.

One-footed on the unsigned auction ledger, the Fool produced a small hot hand-pie from nowhere polite and set it before Mr. BaneWAP with a bow. The whisperer-at-the-throne, the schemer in the sleeve — an old trope, sampled a thousand times. He returned it changed, with interest: in Boon.land the vizier is baked goods, and you can smell exactly what he's been hoarding.

sections.figcaption: Crosswind Council: keys narrow in the open; a wish is too large to file.

content.text: Boof watched the argument cross the pine grain like weather. Boon and bane sat under one shared squall and bargained without declaring war; that was the table's whole genius. But when the clerks brought out the rack of civic keys — iron ones honestly narrowed, brass ones watched for secret growing — not one of them matched the egg. The Genie explained it the way he priced everything, flatly and without pity: a wish is not property, because it is not a thing; it is a redirection of momentum the world already has. You cannot auction a bend in the river. You can only stand where it bends. From beneath the table, Boof could see the parts of the meeting the mirror missed: wet hems, boots braced against the slope, a clerk warming cramped fingers under one arm. Whenever a delegate struck the pine, dust shook loose beside her nose. They wanted the rain kept off their roofs and the paths kept open to their doors; some wanted more, but those wants were there beneath the grander words. She shifted the egg away from a drip. Above her, someone asked who would be responsible for keeping it safe.

None of the keys fitted. The oldest clerk tried the last one, set it down, and wrote: the wish stays with its finder. Rain ticked on the tabletop. Across it, the pie smiled. “And who,” he asked, “inherits from the finder?” Boof's fur lifted along her back. The clerk kept his pen above the page.

content.text: Boof left the hill with the wish she had never asked to hold. Finder, the clerk had written, as if finding were a small thing a dog did with her nose and not a door the world had opened under her paws. The Genie walked beside her, unhurried. "He will not steal it," he said of the pie on the other road. "Stealing costs a miracle. Paperwork costs pocket change, and he knows which one he can afford."

Below the hill, two claims reached the counting room before supper. One named Boof. One called the wish an asset. The clerks pinned them side by side, shut the door, and went home. Under the desk, where no one thought to listen, the floor began to sing.

loreItems.description: Council law: a key may be filed smaller in the open, never grown in secret. A wish is the largest key ever cut — too large for the rack.
Mr. BaneWAP debuts: a pie of hoarded berries gone bitter in a banker's crust. He wants the wish filed, appraised, and auctioned — to himself.
The mirror chamber's truth: BaneWAP is not a foreign villain. He is the reflection of what wanting becomes when it hoards instead of serving slices.
No key covers the egg, so the council cannot rule. The wish stays with its finder. The Fool samples the evil-vizier trope and honks it back as pastry.
